Heavy advertiser, including sports sponsorship, and well known among office and technology workers globally.

NotCo is a Santiago, Chile food technology company using an AI platform called Giuseppe to create plant-based versions of animal-based foods. Its consumer brands include NotMilk, NotBurger, NotMayo and NotIceCream, sold in Latin America, the US and other markets through retailers such as Whole Foods and Walmart, and it also licenses its AI to food manufacturers like Kraft Heinz. Founded in 2015, it raised about 433 million dollars and was valued at 1.5 billion dollars in 2021. Private. Recognized consumer brand in Latin America.

Postman is a San Francisco software company whose API platform helps developers design, test, document and monitor APIs, used by over 35 million developers and 500,000 organizations. It earns money from team and enterprise subscriptions. Founded in 2014 in Bangalore, India, it raised about 433 million dollars, with a 5.6 billion dollar valuation in 2021 led by Insight Partners. It is private. B2B, well known among software developers, with little general consumer awareness.

Qiniu is a Shanghai cloud services company offering cloud storage, content delivery, live video and data processing services, and data lake and analytics tools for apps and enterprises. Customers include internet and media companies and developers across China. Founded in 2011, it raised about 397 million dollars from investors such as Alibaba and Tencent, and filed to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. B2B, with limited public awareness outside China's developer community.

about: Signifyd is a San Jose, California e-commerce fraud protection company. Its platform decides in real time whether online orders are legitimate and guarantees against chargebacks, also handling returns abuse and account takeover. Customers are retailers and brands such as Peloton and Lacoste, who pay per-order fees. Founded in 2011, it raised about 409 million dollars, with a 1.3 billion dollar valuation in 2021. It is private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Vimeo is a New York video software company offering tools for hosting, live streaming, editing and sharing video, used by creators, marketers and businesses. Revenue comes from subscriptions, with around 90 million users and annual revenue near 400 million dollars. Founded in 2004, it was part of IAC, spun off in 2021 and listed on Nasdaq (VMEO). Bending Spoons agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 1.4 billion dollars. Well known among video creators but a modest mainstream brand.

Aviatrix is a Santa Clara, California cloud network security company whose platform provides secure connectivity, visibility and policy enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud. Customers are large enterprises and government bodies that pay subscriptions. Founded in 2014, it has raised about 340 million dollars from investors including Sequoia, Tiger Global and CIT. It is private. B2B, known mainly to cloud and network engineers, with no consumer awareness.

beqom is a Nyon, Switzerland enterprise software company offering cloud tools for compensation management, pay equity and transparency, performance and total rewards. Customers are large multinational employers worldwide such as Zurich, BNP Paribas and Telefonica, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2009, it has raised about 360 million dollars, and in 2024 it was acquired by Visma. It is a B2B HR software brand with little consumer awareness.

about: Cognite is an industrial AI and software company, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona, with its roots in Norway where it was founded in 2016 as an Aker spin-off. Its Cognite Data Fusion platform contextualizes industrial data for asset-heavy sectors such as oil and gas, power, manufacturing and shipping, serving customers like Saudi Aramco, Aker BP and Celanese. Raised about 338 million dollars, with Aker BP, Saudi Aramco and Aker investors. Private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

DataStax is a Santa Clara, California database software company built around Apache Cassandra, offering the Astra DB cloud database and tools for building generative AI applications with vector search, plus Langflow. Customers are enterprises such as Verizon, Home Depot and Capital One. Founded in 2010, it raised about 343 million dollars and was acquired by IBM in 2025. B2B, known among developers and data engineers, with no consumer awareness.

DELFI Diagnostics is a Palo Alto, California cancer detection company based in Baltimore roots at Johns Hopkins, using whole-genome sequencing of cell-free DNA fragments and machine learning to detect cancers, notably lung cancer via a blood test. Customers are clinicians and health systems, and it also partners with pharma. Founded in 2019, it raised about 330 million dollars from investors including Third Rock and Nauta. Private. Healthcare B2B brand with limited public awareness.

about: Drata is a San Francisco compliance automation company whose trust management platform automates evidence collection and continuous monitoring for frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA and GDPR. Customers are technology companies and growing businesses, which pay subscriptions. Founded in 2020, it raised about 328 million dollars, with a 2 billion dollar valuation in 2022. It is private. B2B, with strong awareness among security and compliance teams and little consumer visibility.

HashiCorp is a San Francisco infrastructure software company founded in 2012, known for open source tools Terraform, Vault, Consul, Nomad, Packer and Vagrant used to provision and secure cloud infrastructure. Customers are large enterprises worldwide paying for enterprise and cloud subscriptions, with annual revenue near 600 million dollars. It listed on Nasdaq (HCP) in 2021 and was acquired by IBM in early 2025 for about 6.4 billion dollars. B2B, widely known by developers, with no consumer awareness.

Ironclad is a San Francisco contract lifecycle management software company. Its AI-powered platform handles contract creation, workflow, negotiation, approval and storage for legal, sales and procurement teams, used by customers such as L'Oreal, Mastercard and OpenAI. Founded in 2014, it raised about 334 million dollars, with a 3.2 billion dollar valuation in 2022. It is private. B2B, known to in-house lawyers, with little consumer awareness.

Lattice is a San Francisco people management software company, founded in 2015, whose platform covers performance reviews, goals, engagement surveys, compensation and HRIS, plus AI tools. Customers are thousands of mid-size companies paying per-employee subscriptions. It raised about 330 million dollars, with a 3 billion dollar valuation in 2022. It is private. B2B, with strong awareness among HR leaders and little consumer visibility.

Loadsmart is a Chicago freight technology company with an AI-driven platform that matches shippers with carriers for truckload, intermodal and drayage freight, and offers a transportation management system. Customers are enterprise shippers, brokers and carriers, earning from freight margins and software fees. Founded in 2014, it raised about 346 million dollars, with backers including Maersk and Tiger Global. Private. B2B logistics brand with little consumer awareness.

At-Bay is a San Francisco insurtech that provides cyber insurance and technology errors and omissions coverage for businesses, using security scanning data and risk tools to underwrite and help clients improve defenses. Customers are small to mid-size businesses sold via brokers. Founded in 2016, it raised about 296 million dollars with a 1.35 billion dollar valuation in 2021. Private. B2B insurance brand with limited consumer awareness.

BigPanda is a Redwood City, California software company with an AIOps platform that correlates alerts across IT monitoring tools and automates incident response for large IT operations teams. Customers include enterprises and telecoms like Intel and Cisco, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2012 in Israel and the US, it raised about 313 million dollars, with a 1.2 billion dollar valuation in 2021 led by Insight Partners. Private. B2B, well known only to IT operations teams.

Matillion is a Salford, UK data integration software company, founded in Manchester in 2011, whose cloud-native platform loads and transforms data into warehouses such as Snowflake, Databricks, Amazon Redshift and Google BigQuery. Customers are enterprises worldwide paying subscriptions. It also has a major presence in Denver. It raised about 290 million dollars, valued around 1.5 billion dollars in 2021. Private. B2B, known among data engineers, with little consumer awareness.

Sensors Data is a Beijing customer data and analytics platform company, founded in 2015, offering behavioral analytics, customer data platforms and marketing automation, often deployed privately inside the customer's own servers so companies can analyze user data securely. Customers are Chinese banks, retailers, internet firms and manufacturers, paying software and service fees. It raised about 290 million dollars. Private. B2B, with little awareness outside China's enterprise technology market.

Sky Mavis is a technology company, headquartered in Singapore with its roots in Vietnam, that created Axie Infinity, the blockchain play-to-earn game, plus the Ronin network and wallet. Revenue came from in-game marketplace fees and token sales. Axie Infinity peaked in 2021 with millions of players, and the Ronin bridge was hacked for about 600 million dollars in 2022. It raised about 311 million dollars, valued at 3 billion dollars in 2021. Private. Known among crypto gamers, with fading mass awareness.

Staffbase is a German employee communications software company, founded in 2014 in Chemnitz and with offices including Berlin and New York. Its Staffbase Employee Communications Platform provides intranets, employee apps, email and analytics for large enterprises with frontline workers, with customers such as Audi, Adidas and Deutsche Bahn. It raised about 306 million dollars, with a 1 billion dollar valuation in 2022. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

Versa Networks is a Santa Clara, California networking and security company offering SASE, SD-WAN and secure access service edge software, which converges WAN connectivity and cloud security for enterprises and service providers. Customers include large corporations, telecoms and managed service providers, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2012, it raised about 316 million dollars and is valued above 1 billion dollars. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

XSKY Data Technology is a Beijing company focused on software-defined storage, offering distributed block, file and object storage plus data lake and cloud infrastructure products for enterprise data centers. Customers are Chinese banks, telecoms, internet companies and manufacturers, who buy software licenses and support. Founded in 2015, it raised about 284 million dollars from Chinese venture investors. Private. B2B infrastructure vendor, with no consumer awareness and little visibility outside China.

about: ZeroFox is a Baltimore, Maryland cybersecurity company that provides external cybersecurity: digital risk protection, threat intelligence and attack surface management to defend brands and people from threats on social media, the web and the dark web. Customers are enterprises and governments. Founded in 2013, it went public via a SPAC merger in 2022 on Nasdaq (ZFOX) and was taken private by Haveli Investments in 2024. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

Pilot is a San Francisco company that provides bookkeeping, tax preparation and CFO services for startups and small businesses, combining software with human accountants. Customers are tech startups and small firms, paying monthly fees. Founded in 2017, it raised about 172 million dollars, with a 1.2 billion dollar valuation in 2021. Private. B2B, known among startup founders, with limited consumer awareness.

Aibee is a Beijing artificial intelligence company founded in 2017 that develops computer vision, speech recognition and data analysis technology for retail, shopping malls and commercial real estate, such as customer flow analysis, smart store management and marketing. Customers are mall operators, retailers and property companies, mainly in China. It raised about 273 million dollars across several funding rounds. Private. B2B technology supplier, with no consumer awareness.

Founded in 2012, it raised around 255 million dollars, including a growth investment led by private equity. It is private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

about: Exela Technologies is an Irving, Texas business process automation company offering document processing, digital mailroom, healthcare claims, payment and accounts payable services, plus software. Customers are banks, insurers, healthcare and government clients, mostly in the US and Europe. It listed on Nasdaq (XELA) via a 2017 SPAC merger with Quinpario, with revenue around 1 billion dollars in earlier years, then restructured. It has high debt and its stock has been delisted or distressed. B2B, little consumer awareness.

Firebolt is a cloud data warehouse company, based in Palo Alto, California, offering a high-performance analytics database for data-intensive applications. Its product is aimed at data engineers building customer-facing analytics. Founded in 2019 in Israel by former Sisense executives, it raised about 264 million dollars, with a 1.4 billion dollar valuation in 2022. Private. B2B, known among data engineers, with no consumer awareness.

Firework is a San Mateo, California company providing livestream shopping and short video technology for retailers and publishers, letting brands embed interactive videos and live commerce on their websites and apps. Customers are retailers and media companies, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2019 as Loop Now, it is backed by NEA, Wing and Singtel Innov8, raising about 269 million dollars. Private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Customers are retailers and consumer brands in the US. Founded in 2013, it raised about 263 million dollars, and in 2024 it was acquired by Odyssey Logistics. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

Customers are investment banks and capital markets firms, paying software subscriptions and services. about: Opn, formerly Omise, is a payment platform headquartered in Tokyo, with major operations in Thailand, Japan, Singapore and Malaysia. It offers an online payment gateway, point-of-sale, payouts, crypto-related services and a payment management platform for merchants, earning transaction fees. Founded in 2013, it raised about 260 million dollars from investors including SBI Group. Private. B2B, known among e-commerce merchants in Southeast Asia, with limited consumer awareness.

about: Productboard is a San Francisco product management software company, founded in 2014 in Prague, whose platform helps product teams collect customer feedback, plan roadmaps and prioritize features, with AI assistance. Customers are software firms and technology teams such as Zoom and Microsoft, paying subscriptions. It raised about 262 million dollars, with a 1.7 billion dollar valuation in 2021. Private. B2B, known among product managers, with no consumer awareness.

Rapid, known as RapidAPI, is a San Francisco company that runs the world's largest API marketplace and developer platform, letting developers discover, test and connect to APIs, plus enterprise API hubs. Founded in 2015, it raised about 272 million dollars, and was acquired by Nokia in 2024. Customers are developers and enterprises. B2B, known to software developers, with no consumer awareness.

Salt Security is a Palo Alto, California API security company, with an Israeli R&D base. Its platform uses AI to discover APIs, detect attacks and block threats for enterprises. Customers are large companies in finance, retail and technology. Founded in 2016, it raised about 271 million dollars, with a valuation of 1.4 billion dollars in 2022. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.
